Discourse on Comets.fact: Grassi replied in 1626 with Ratio ponderum librae et simbellae, which focused on doctrinal issues rather than scientific questions.

Discourse on Comets.subject: Applied Sciences
Discourse on Comets.question: Having defeated _____ on the points he considered important, Galileo declined to publish anything further on the topic
Discourse on Comets.fact: Galileo's final response in the dispute with Grassi was Il Saggiatore (The Assayer), which he published in 1623. Grassi replied in 1626 with Ratio ponderum librae et simbellae, which focused on doctrinal issues rather than scientific questions.

Discourse on Comets.subject: Applied Sciences
Discourse on Comets.question: While the _____ dei Lincei were considering what tone a reply from Galileo ought to take, Guiducci replied directly to Grassi in the Spring of 1620
Discourse on Comets.fact: While the Accademia dei Lincei were considering what tone a reply from Galileo ought to take, Guiducci replied directly to Grassi in the Spring of 1620. Discourse on Comets.subject: Applied Sciences
Discourse on Comets.question: Galileo was very pleased with _____'s efforts, proposing him for membership of the Accademia dei Lincei in May 1621 (although he did not actually become a member until 1625)
Discourse on Comets.fact: While the Accademia dei Lincei were considering what tone a reply from Galileo ought to take, Guiducci replied directly to Grassi in the Spring of 1620. Guiducci countered the various arguments Grassi had put forward against Galileo, describing some of Grassi's experiments as 'full of errors and not without a hint of fraud.' Guiducci concluded with an attempt to reconcile experimental evidence with theological arguments, but firmly asserted the primacy of data gathered through observation.

Discourse on the Method.subject: Applied Sciences
Discourse on the Method.question: The _____ was 1637 treatise by Descartes.
Discourse on the Method.fact: Discourse on the Method of Rightly Conducting One's Reason and of Seeking Truth in the Sciences (French: Discours de la Méthode pour bien conduire sa raison, et chercher la vérité dans les sciences) is a philosophical and autobiographical treatise published by René Descartes in 1637. Discourse on the Method is one of the most influential works in the history of modern philosophy, and important to the development of natural sciences.

Discourse on the Method.subject: Applied Sciences
Discourse on the Method.question: It is best known as the source of the famous quotation "Je pense, donc je suis" ("I think, therefore I am", or "I am thinking, therefore I exist"), which occurs in _____ of the work
Discourse on the Method.fact: It is best called the source of the famous quotation "Je pense, donc je suis" ("I think, therefore I am", or "I am thinking, therefore I exist"), which occurs in Part IV of the work.

Discourse on the Method.subject: Applied Sciences
Discourse on the Method.question: A similar argument without this precise wording is found in Meditations on First Philosophy (_____), and a Latin version of the same statement, "Cogito, ergo sum", is found in Principles of Philosophy
Discourse on the Method.fact: A similar argument without this precise wording is found in Meditations on First Philosophy (1641), and a Latin version of the same statement, "Cogito, ergo sum", is found in Principles of Philosophy (1644).

Discourse on the Method.subject: Applied Sciences
Discourse on the Method.question: In this work, _____ tackles the problem of skepticism, which had previously been studied by other philosophers
Discourse on the Method.fact: In this work, Descartes tackles the problem of skepticism, which had previously been studied by other philosophers. While addressing some of his predecessors and contemporaries, Descartes modified their approach to account for a truth he found to be incontrovertible; he started his line of reasoning by doubting everything, so as to assess the world from a fresh perspective, clear of any preconceived notions.

Discourse on the Method.subject: Applied Sciences

Discourse on the Method.fact: The book was originally published in Leiden, in the Netherlands.

Discourse on the Method.fact: Later, it was translated into Latin (Dissertatio de Methodo recte utendi ratione, et veritatem in scientiis investigandi) and published in 1656 in Amsterdam.

Discourse on the Method.subject: Applied Sciences

Discourse on the Method.fact: Together with Meditations on First Philosophy, Principles of Philosophy and Rules for the Direction of the Mind, it forms the base of the epistemology called Cartesianism.

Discourse on the Tides.subject: Applied Sciences
Discourse on the Tides.question: The _____ was Essay by Galileo Galilei.
Discourse on the Tides.fact: "Discourse on the Tides" (Italian: Discorso Sul Flusso E Il Reflusso Del Mare) is an essay written by Galileo Galilei in 1616 as a letter to Alessandro Orsini that attempted to explain the motion of Earth's tides as a consequence of Earth's rotation and revolution around the Sun.

Discourse on the Tides.subject: Applied Sciences
Discourse on the Tides.question: The same ideas form an important part of Galileo's Dialogue Concerning the _____
Discourse on the Tides.fact: The same ideas form an important part of Galileo's Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems. The letter is thus not just an explanation of tidal phenomenon but also a private confirmation and defense of Galileo's ideas on heliocentrism, which are discussed completely in his Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems.

Discourse on the Tides.fact: Galileo's ideas for tidal theory may have begun during 1595.
